scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
product_from_film: Bits shows setting up Klaus, a team assistant powered by OpenClaw, and connecting it to Slack.
explains_well: The final Slack question receives a specific Hacker News answer after an earlier access-not-configured message.
unclear: The fast desktop recording has no step labels, so the difference between instance creation, device pairing, Slack installation and user approval is hard to follow.
scenario: Create an assistant instance, approve connections and ask a question in Slack.
product_clear_basis: The readable setup page names Klaus as an AI assistant for a team powered by OpenClaw.

scenes.action: A Bits Klaus page starts an instance setup. Status changes while a large stopwatch advances beside the browser; the view briefly switches to a dark OpenClaw chat and back.
scenes.design: Uncropped desktop, forest wallpaper, browser and separate stopwatch.
scenes.purpose: Present a timed setup with waiting compressed.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 0–11s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A pending pairing request appears with approval controls and a paired-device list. The recording switches to the OpenClaw chat, where a message is entered, then returns to the setup page.
scenes.design: Light setup page contrasted with dark chat.
scenes.purpose: Show device pairing and the first chat interaction.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 11–20s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A Slack App Installation page opens, followed by Slack permission approval. The view returns to Klaus integration and device information, then the Slack app opens.

scenes.purpose: Connect the assistant to a workspace.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 20–31s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A Slack direct message is sent and a reply appears. The view switches back to the web chat, where more text is entered and responses appear.
scenes.design: Overlapping Slack and browser windows with a continuing stopwatch.
scenes.purpose: Resolve setup and access steps; the fast switching obscures their exact relationship.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 31–46s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Slack returns. An earlier OpenClaw access-not-configured response includes pairing instructions. A later question asks for the top Hacker News story and Klaus replies with a title, points, comments and link. The stopwatch is stopped around 3 min 21 s.
scenes.design: Slack conversation foreground, web chat behind and large timer at right.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate a working final exchange and the displayed setup time.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 46–55.766s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.
